newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds jump on U.S. economic indicators.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds jump on U.S. economic indicators.

text.p: Argentine bonds rallied Tuesday on favorable U.S. key economic indicators but traders recommended caution as more data is due out this week.

"The market started out really firm after U.S. indicators pushed interest rates down," said one trader at a local bank. "But let's watch out. We will have more indicators coming out of the United States every day of the week now."
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 5/8 at 91-3/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 rose $0.10 to 126.10.

The U.S. government said its Employment Cost Index rose just 0.6 percent in the first quarter, less than the 0.9 percent rise that economists had forecast. Durable goods orders in March, which economists had expected to be flat, fell 3.0 percent, while February orders, originally reported as having been up 1.5 percent, were revised to just at 0.8 percent increase.
But more U.S. economic data is expected to be released this week prompting local traders to remain cautious.
"At these prices investors want some confirmation that the data will be good throughout before they go on a buying spree," said one trader at a foreign bank.
"Nobody likes to pay top prices unless they are sure it's worth it," he added.
